pack.title: Saying no
pack.description: The complete sentence. No is a full answer that needs no apology tour.

scenarios.setting: Work. Your manager adds a Friday project to your full week.
scenarios.jab: Can you just take this on? It'll be quick.

replies.line: My week is full. Which task should move to make room?
replies.why: It asks for prioritization instead of pretending every task can fit.
replies.delivery: Name the time limit, pause, and let the manager choose what changes.

replies.line: Which task moves if I take this?
replies.why: It identifies the tradeoff rather than committing to an invented date.
replies.delivery: Name the time limit, pause, and let the manager choose what changes.

replies.line: I'd love to help — my week's genuinely full. What can slide?
replies.why: Willingness plus the real constraint invites them to prioritize with you.
replies.delivery: Name the time limit, pause, and let the manager choose what changes.

replies.why: Letting the calendar object keeps your hands clean and the no obvious.
replies.delivery: Name the time limit, pause, and let the manager choose what changes.

trap.line: Ugh, fine — but this is the last time.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Discuss priorities when more work exceeds your capacity.

followUp.line: Then I need your help deciding what moves; I can't finish all of it today.
followUp.why: It makes the capacity constraint explicit and asks for prioritization.
followUp.delivery: Name the time limit, pause, and let the manager choose what changes.

scenarios.setting: Friend's wedding planning. You're asked to be in the tenth event.
scenarios.jab: You HAVE to come to the engagement brunch too. Everyone's coming.

replies.line: I'll be at the wedding, fully present. Skipping brunch.
replies.why: It names what you're giving before what you're not, so the no lands inside a yes.
replies.delivery: Keep the warmth genuine and the refusal clear; avoid promising to celebrate extra to compensate.

replies.line: I'm skipping brunch. See you at the wedding.
replies.why: It declines the specific event while confirming attendance you already intend.
replies.delivery: Keep the warmth genuine and the refusal clear; avoid promising to celebrate extra to compensate.

replies.line: I'm looking forward to the wedding; I won't be able to join the brunch.
replies.why: It expresses care without promising extra effort to compensate.
replies.delivery: Keep the warmth genuine and the refusal clear; avoid promising to celebrate extra to compensate.

replies.line: I'm on the wedding roster, not the brunch roster.
replies.why: The light distinction makes the attendance boundary clear.
replies.delivery: Keep the warmth genuine and the refusal clear; avoid promising to celebrate extra to compensate.

scenarios.goal: Decline one event without withdrawing support.

followUp.jab: Everyone else is making the effort.
followUp.line: I care about celebrating with you; I won't be at the brunch.
followUp.why: It states care and the specific attendance decision without comparing guests.
followUp.delivery: Keep the warmth genuine and the refusal clear; avoid promising to celebrate extra to compensate.

scenarios.setting: Family call. Your parents want every holiday at their house, forever.
scenarios.jab: After everything we do, you can't even come for Christmas?

replies.line: Our plans this year are set. I know you're disappointed.
replies.why: It states the plan while acknowledging the feeling without inventing an agreed rotation.
replies.delivery: Pause after acknowledging disappointment; keep the plan matter-of-fact.

replies.line: We're keeping our plans this year.
replies.why: It makes the current decision clear without implying a nonexistent agreement.
replies.delivery: Pause after acknowledging disappointment; keep the plan matter-of-fact.

replies.line: I wish we could clone December — we'd spend it all with you.
replies.why: Wishing alongside them shows the love the guilt claims is missing.
replies.delivery: Pause after acknowledging disappointment; keep the plan matter-of-fact.

replies.line: Our holiday calendar is fully booked this year.
replies.why: A mild image holds the plan without mocking disappointment.
replies.delivery: Pause after acknowledging disappointment; keep the plan matter-of-fact.

trap.line: Fine, we'll come. But don't expect us to enjoy it.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Hold an agreed holiday plan under guilt.

followUp.line: I know you're disappointed; our plan this year is staying the same.
followUp.why: It acknowledges the feeling without treating it as a decision you must reverse.
followUp.delivery: Pause after acknowledging disappointment; keep the plan matter-of-fact.

scenarios.setting: A volunteer organizer repeatedly asks you to lead another event.
scenarios.jab: You're the only person who can do this properly.
scenarios.goal: Decline a role despite flattering pressure.

replies.line: I won't lead this one. Please find another organizer.
replies.why: It declines the role without accepting praise as an obligation.
replies.delivery: Thank them sincerely, keep the refusal short, and avoid offering a smaller role you cannot sustain.

replies.why: It answers the assignment request without negotiating your value to the group.
replies.delivery: Thank them sincerely, keep the refusal short, and avoid offering a smaller role you cannot sustain.

replies.line: Thank you for trusting me; I don't have capacity to lead this event.
replies.why: It receives the compliment while making your capacity clear.
replies.delivery: Thank them sincerely, keep the refusal short, and avoid offering a smaller role you cannot sustain.

replies.line: My organizing hat is taking this event off.
replies.why: The joke concerns your workload rather than the organizer's need.
replies.delivery: Thank them sincerely, keep the refusal short, and avoid offering a smaller role you cannot sustain.

followUp.jab: Can you at least supervise everything?
followUp.line: I can't take responsibility for this event in another form either.
followUp.why: It recognizes that a renamed role can carry the same commitment.
followUp.delivery: Thank them sincerely, keep the refusal short, and avoid offering a smaller role you cannot sustain.
